 4 robbers fall in Taguig as PNP keeps up crime-fighting efforts amid ASEAN Summit
 by 
 Christopher Lloyd Caliwan
 Nov 17, 2026
 2:48 PM GMT+8
 ENFORCING THE LAW . Taguig City police personnel conduct an operation in Barangay Sta.  Ana on Nov. 16, 2026, which resulted in the arrest of four individuals and the recovery of three motorcycles and two firearms. The Philippine National Police said Tuesday (Nov. 17) that despite committing thousands of personnel to secure the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits, it continued its daily efforts to prevent crime and enforce the law. (Photo courtesy of Southern Police District) 
 MANILA – Despite committing thousands of personnel to secure the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits, the Philippine National Police (PNP) continued its daily efforts to prevent crime and enforce the law.
 This was demonstrated in a police operation in Barangay Sta. Ana, Taguig City on Monday, where personnel of the Taguig City Police Station Intelligence Section arrested four robbery suspects and seized three motorcycles and two firearms.
 “Our tight schedule to secure delegates and summit venues will not be at the expense of our mandate to maintain peace and order that includes sustaining our campaign against criminal elements,” PNP Chief Gen. Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. said in a statement on Tuesday.  
 This is in line with the directive of President Ferdinand R. Marcos, Jr., through the guidance of Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla, to maintain peace and order, intensify police presence in communities, and prevent criminal activities amid the country’s hosting of the ASEAN Summit.
 Southern Police District (SPD) Director Brig. Gen. Rodel Pastor commended the operating personnel for their prompt response, coordination, and determination in pursuing the suspects despite the armed confrontation.
 “Criminals who threaten the safety of our communities must be held accountable. Our personnel remain committed to pursuing every lead, gathering the necessary evidence, and bringing those responsible before the law. We will continue to strengthen intelligence-driven operations and uphold our TSAPA principles – Trustworthy, Service-oriented, Accessible, Professional, and Accountable – in protecting the public,” Pastor said in a separate statement.
 On Nov. 12, two robbery suspects were neutralized in a shootout with police officers after they allegedly robbed another police officer who was conducting surveillance operations in Barangay Ususan, Taguig City.
 The suspects reportedly attempted to flee when confronted by police, prompting officers to open fire and triggering a brief gun battle. A responding police officer was injured.
 Police investigators are now establishing the link between the four arrested suspects and the two others who died in the Nov. 12 firefight in the same city.
 “This operation proves that while your PNP is busy in its obligation for the ASEAN Summit, our crime prevention and law enforcement measures remain in place to secure communities and keep everyone safe,” Nartatez said.
 The arrest came amid heightened police security preparations for the ASEAN Summit, which required the deployment of thousands of personnel to protect visiting foreign leaders, delegates, and other participants.
 Nartatez earlier assured the public that the PNP will keep a sufficient number of personnel to carry out the daily operations of the police, such as police visibility and strategic operations against criminal elements, despite ASEAN Summit security commitments.
 He said that such security commitments should not leave communities with inadequate police coverage.
 “This important event will not affect our daily task of protecting our communities from any form of threats,” he said. (PNA)
